newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut stocks fall as market consolidates.
newsitem.headline: Beirut stocks fall as market consolidates.

text.p: Most of the leading shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange fell on Tuesday in relatively quiet trade and brokers said the market was in a consolidating mood.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.97 percent to 154.21. The LISPI general index fell 0.37 percent to 89.59 and the BLOM general index fell 0.97 percent to 926.42.
Turnover rose to 234,570 shares from 108,892 on Monday and value also rose to $1,584,697 from $901,326 but both were still well below recent levels.
Of the eight listed companies, four shares fell, one was unchanged, three were not traded and bloc trades only were reported for two.
"Being quiet is not a negative sign especially when the market is consolidating," a broker, who wished not to be identified, said.
Two of the three bank shares slipped from their alltime highs on profit-taking while Solidere shares fell on low turnover.
Bank of Beirut slipped to $3.9375 from $4 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce dropped to $18.25 from $18.5. Banque Audi was unchanged at its record high of $23.125.
"Everyone is waiting for the banks' second quarter results. There is a strong feeling BLC and Audi would rise. BOB is also expected to increase," the broker said.
He said only 34,716 of BLC's 1.29 million listed shares traded and only 13,102 Audi shares traded out of 4.16 million listed.
Solidere A fell to $10.375 from $10.50 and B fell to $10.75 from $10.875 on turnover of 30,341 shares. Demand for both shares was strong but brokers said mismatching on prices kept volume down.
"People want to buy at low prices and sell at high prices. Everyone knows the share is undervalued. I expect some matching by the end of the month and the stock would then rise," the broker said.

Of the four listed industrial firms, some 50,000 Ciments Libanais traded in bloc on the floor at $1.28125 and bloc of 80,275 Eternit shares traded on the floor at $2. There was no price fixing for the shares on Tuesday.
There was no trade in Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
